newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian call money back up 50 bps to 10.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian call money back up 50 bps to 10.5 pct.

text.p: Croatian call money rate rose to 10.5 percent on Friday amid slightly strained end-of-week liquidity following Thursday's fall to 10 percent, dealers said.
"The money market is experiencing a strong demand for kuna funds, but this is not matched by the money on offer," a dealer told Reuters.
She added that pension payments by local banks caused their strong demand today.
Fresh trade totalled 42.5 million kuna and all the deals were call money at 10.5 percent, back up 50 basis points.
Two banks borrowed 29 milllion kuna in overnight trade on Thursday to cover their shortfalls and maintain mandatory reserves. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
